hook_text: A new business had over one hundred thousand rand land in its account in month one. It had earned less than a fifth of that.
clip_script: March at a repair shop: one hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty rand into the bank. Looks like a boom. Now read the cash receipts journal like an accountant. Sixty thousand: the owner's own savings, capital. Twenty-five thousand: a bank loan, which means a liability, money that must go back. Only eighteen thousand five hundred and fifty was actually earned. Every CRJ line makes assets go up; the name tag decides the rest. Current income or rent: owner's equity up, earned. Capital: owner's equity up, but not earned. Loan: liabilities up. Then April: thirty-one thousand three hundred and thirty in, twenty-one thousand three hundred and thirty of it earned, no borrowing. Smaller number, healthier story. Bank balance is not profit.
visual_style: A whiteboard bank app showing a big number, then the number breaking into three coloured blocks labelled capital, loan and earned, beside a level equation scale.
mood: Eye-opening and slightly contrarian, a reality check on big balances.
pacing: Big reveal up front, a quick three-way split, a calm comparison with April, a sharp last line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read any cash journal like an accountant.
